papers.title_en: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback
papers.authors: Li Wang, Chen Zhang, Yirong Yang, Xingyu Chen, Jinkun Zhao, Tianhao Peng, Wenjun Wu
papers.evidence: 通过反馈优化可重用的个性化技能
papers.tldr: 本文针对大语言模型在利用用户反馈学习个性化技能时容易混入请求特定修正导致负迁移的问题，提出了一种名为SkillGrain的框架。该框架将反馈分解为原子规则并预测其可迁移性，通过强化学习联合优化技能归纳与生成，实现对持久化偏好的选择性保留，从而提升跨请求的个性化泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: User feedback enables LLMs to refine reusable personalized skills, but often mixes persistent preferences with request-specific corrections. Indiscriminately retaining both risks negative transfer, motivating selective retention at the level of individual requirements. We frame this challenge as selective transfer over atomic rules and propose SkillGrain, a framework for learning reusable personalized skills from user feedback. SkillGrain decomposes feedback into independently actionable rules, predicts their transferability, and retains only those suitable for future requests. To learn these decisions, we combine rubric-guided skill rewards with fine-grained credit assignment that separately evaluates rule content and retention decisions. We further jointly optimize skill induction and skill-conditioned generation through reinforcement learning, ensuring that learned skills support downstream personalization. We construct a benchmark spanning five personalized writing tasks to evaluate cross-request generalization. Experiments across three base models in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings show that SkillGrain achieves the best overall average performance among competing methods.

papers.title_en: Ranking and Partitioning of Attention Heads for Sparse and Continual Reinforcement Learning Fine-tuning
papers.authors: Ruizhe Shi, Zaiwen Yang, Qiubo Wang, Banghua Zhu, Maryam Fazel
papers.evidence: 语言模型的稀疏强化学习微调
papers.tldr: 本文研究了语言模型在稀疏和持续强化学习微调中的注意力头排序与划分方法。通过梯度范数对注意力头进行排序以选择关键子集进行稀疏训练，并在多任务间划分注意力头以减少干扰和保持能力。实验表明，该方法在数学、指令遵循和编码任务上表现优异，能有效平衡适应新任务与保持旧能力。
papers.abstract_en: We study sparse and continual reinforcement learning fine-tuning of language models through attention-head ranking and partitioning. For sparse learning, we rank attention heads by gradient norm to identify a small subset of heads that can be trained effectively. For continual learning, we partition heads across tasks to reduce cross-task interference and preserve previously learned capabilities. Theoretically, we relate gradient norm to training effectiveness, and further characterize why sparse, separated head updates can remain stable. Empirically, across math, instruction-following, and coding tasks, tuning higher-ranked heads consistently outperforms tuning lower-ranked ones while often matching denser baselines, and head partitioning improves retention while preserving adaptation to new tasks.
